correctness.rationale: Tan weight restriction gives nonzero code weights 12 or 15 in length17, and ternary Griesmer rules out rank3 (12+4+2=18>17). The two 12-supports meet7, so their union is all17 and no generator column is zero. Each of 17 nonzero columns is nonzero for 3 of the 4 projective characters, so the character weights sum 51; with two weight12 words the remainder is 12+15. Their complementary zero sets give four column multiplicities 5,5,5,2; independent exhaustive F3 code enumeration checked all 9 words. Using simply connected minimal resolution, the boundary/localization sequence identifies cusp code with H^1 of the smooth locus; nonzero inertia at every A2 singularity makes the maximal connected 3^2 cover normalize to a smooth surface with three preimages at each cusp. Euler e(S)=55-34=21 and e(Y)=9(21-17)+3*17=87; unramified codimension-one K²=9*5=45, Noether chi=11, and Tan intermediate cyclic quotient pg values (6,6,6,4), q=0 yield pgY=10,qY=0 through the four-subgroup character identity. The checker verifies only combinatorial/numerical data, not complex cover geometry; the latter rests on the detailed cohomological proof and stated primary-source theorems.

value.rationale: The two intersecting divisible cusp structures of a naturally studied 17-cusp quintic family force an otherwise hidden third twelve-support structure, a distinguished omitted cusp pair, and a smooth canonically polarized ninefold abelian surface with a complete fixed-point profile. This is a motivated geometric classification and simultaneous global invariant package, not a mere isolated arithmetic substitution; it does not claim a new defining quintic.

final_claim: For complex normal quintics with 17 A2 cusps and two independent 12-support cusp-codewords intersecting in seven cusps, the full ternary code has rank 2 and nonzero weights 12,12,12,15 up to sign, column multiplicities 5,5,5,2. Its connected smooth degree-9 (Z/3)^2 cover has K^2=45, pg=10, q=0, c2=87, chi=11, and four nonidentity order-3 fixed-point counts 15,15,15,6.
